This shows how machine learning and bioinformatics convergence can bring remarkable progress in predictive analytics.

articleTitle: Comparison of Various Vision-Language Models: Datasets, Architectures, And Metrics
abstract: We aim to provide a thorough comparison of different vision-language models for the picture captioning task, on several datasets, such as COCO, Flickr8k, and MS COCO. In particular, we analyse the CNN-RNN, CNN-Transformer, Vision Transformer (ViT) + Transformer Decoder, Convolutional Sequenceto Sequence (ConvS2S), and Cross-modal Transformers (like Oscar) Encoder-Decoder architectures. In future work, we intend to train and test these models on a range of datasets in order to assess their potential accuracy and effectiveness in generating descriptive captions. Important metrics including BLEU, METEOR, and CIDEr scores could be used in the evaluation process to provide light on the advantages and disadvantages of each model-dataset combination. The results of this research are meant to direct the choice of ideal structures for particular image captioning jobs, advancing personalized and adaptive image description systems, especially for visually challenged users.

articleTitle: Automated Bone Fracture Detection using YOLOv8
abstract: In medical diagnostics, detection of bone fracture is very crucial. It require time and accurate treatment of that injuries. Previous methods for bone fracture detection are X-ray in which analyzes the fracture by the help of radiations. It is time consuming and prone to human error. To address these limitations we used an automated approach for detection of bone fracture is yolov8. It is deep learning model for real time object detection. Its well suited for medical imagining because its architecture give more accuracy and speed. Our results show YOLOv8 achieve high accuracy and speed from the traditional methods. It is also more reliable. Since it is less time consuming and give the consistent results so it can be used in healthcare. It is possible that its efficiency can be enhance, minimize errors. This study shows the potential of deep learning model like YOLOv8 in diagnostics and medical imaging particularly in bone fracture detection

articleTitle: Enhancing Emergency Response with Cloud-Based Access to Patient Medical Histories
abstract: It's necessary to obtain a patient's medical history to provide timely and effective care in emergency medical situations. However, it may be challenging to obtain the information in case the patient is unconscious or cannot communicate on their own. In this article, we present a safe approach for patient medical history access in situations involving human error. To securely access and decrypt a patient's medical records from a centralized database, our system employs a doctor's decryption key. The encryption strategy, access strategies, and communication protocols form some of the implementation details of this system we discuss. Also, presented a case study that demonstrates just how effective our approach is for real emergency applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Early Detection of Parkinson's Disease with Machine Learning: Insights from Xception Architecture and Random Forest Classifier
abstract: The degenerative neurological disorder known as Parkinson's disease impacts millions of people around the globe. Lack of dopamine, a substance that helps brain neurons communicate, causes the onset of Parkinson's disease. Symptoms of movement dysfunction in Parkinson's disease include when 60-80% of these cells die, preventing dopamine production. Parkinson's disease treatment requires early and accurate diagnosis. Machine learning algorithms can identify clinical data linkages and patterns doctors may overlook. Early identification and treatment of Parkinson's disease can benefit from machine learning for sickness prediction. This research uses xception architecture and the Random Forest Classifier to predict Parkinson's onset. This experiment used UCI ML repository electronic medical records for clinical data. The model had 100% Train Accuracy and 97% Test Accuracy. These findings suggest machine learning can diagnose and forecast Parkinson's disease. This project shows findings on Parkinson's disease diagnosis. Python libraries sci-kit-learn/tensor flow, NumPy, pandas, matplotlib, Keras, etc. will improve our model's accuracy. Using exception architecture and a Random Forest Classifier, we will build a model.

articleTitle: Energy-Efficient Monitoring of Industrial Processes Using IoT Sensors and Predictive Algorithms
abstract: Industrial processes are becoming increasingly complex and larger in scale, which has resulted in a constantly growing demand for robust, scalable monitoring systems. Conventional monitoring strategies entail a huge quantity of sensors and steep infrastructure charges, main to excessive electricity intake and operational costs. Burkhard Theen, vice president at weather analytics company Iteris describes a smart monitoring device using IoT sensors and predictive algorithms for accurately tracking industrial processes on this track. The system is made using a low-voltage IoT sensor community at essential points within the process, which constantly collects and transmits statistics in real time. This data is then fed into the predictive algorithms that use machine learning techniques to analyze and determine any anomalies in the system. The system helps to improve process performance and reduce power consumption by identifying & addressing potential issues at their early stages.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Approach to Detect Disease in Tomato Plants
abstract: Tomatoes are among the most valuable crops in the world. They fall victim to diseases almost every time, which has a devastating effect on yield and quality. Early and accurate illness identification is crucial for sustainable farming practices since it reduces economic losses. This study investigated the possibility of using machine learning models to detect tomato plant diseases using a structured dataset that contains morphological and environmental variables, such as the number of leaf spots, the leaf color index, temperature, and humidity. To find the best supervised learning model for this specific classification job, we examined Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbor, and Support Vector Machine. Feature selection, label encoding, and dataset scaling were all part of the preprocessing.

articleTitle: An Analysis of Generative Adversarial Networks for Intrusion Detection System
abstract: Intrusion Detection System (IDS) is an important part of networks that checks network traffic and identifies mistrustful activity. IDS can be software applications, specialised hardware devices or cloud services. They use one or both of two primary methods to detect threats: signature-based or anomaly-based detection. Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) are machine learning mechanisms that have been used to develop training examples for Intrusion Detection Systems (IDSs). GAN s are adversarial because they train two networks against each other, one of which generates new data and the other predicts whether the data comes from the original data set. GANs are increasingly used in cyber security, especially for tasks that require training on unbalanced data sets of attack classes.

articleTitle: Vision to Voice: An Advanced Blind Assistance System Integrating YOLOv3 and OCR Technologies for Enhanced Mobility
abstract: The rise in need for assistive technologies has led to the development of AI-empowered solutions for better accessibility for visually impaired persons. The proposed system is the use of a real-time object and text detection application using a combination of deep learning and speech synthesis techniques to enhance mobility and independence. The system utilizes Tesseract OCR for text recognition and pyttsx3 for TTS for better interfacing with the environment. YOLOv3-based object detection towards improving environmental awareness involves real-time identification of objects, with confidence thresholding and NMS serving to enhance robustness of the overall detection by curbing false positives. Further, the distance estimation module helps in mobility as it provides information on how far one is situated from an object. This architecture is a hardware-independent, lowlatency, and highly scalable solution compared to conventional assistive systems; thus, such systems are more harmonized for practical applications. Experimental findings exhibited its very high accuracy, confident standing across situations, and enhanced user experience rendering it with huge potential for granting enhanced independence and safety for the visually challenged user base.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Malware Analysis to Strengthen an Antivirus System
abstract: Malware detection remains a paramount challenge in cyber security due to malware's evolving nature and limitations in traditional detection techniques. This paper compares two deep learning models, an LSTM network and a Feed-Forward Neural Network (FFNN), for malware classification. The dataset comprises various features extracted from software samples, which are preprocessed and fed into the models for training and evaluation. The FFNN shows an accuracy of 99.96%, but the LSTM model, leveraging its capability to learn temporal dependencies, achieved an impressive accuracy of 99.989% on the first test. After changing the LSTM hyperparameters, 99.996% accuracy is achieved on the test set with performance improvement to 3 % compared to FFNN. This study highlights the potential of deep learning approaches in enhancing malware detection systems and provides insights into their implementation and performance.

articleTitle: Integrating IoT and Cloud Computing with Smart Irrigation System
abstract: According to an FAO report by 2050, the population may rise to 9 billion, and 9 billion people approx. 60%more plant-based food is required which is obtained by agriculture. In the current scenario 70%of the fresh water is being used in agricultural irrigation. To obtain more food and to increase the productivity of agriculture, irrigation needs to be managed properly using technologies. The study is about the integration of the IoT and cloud computing to make irrigation smart. The smart irrigation system reduces the wastage of water due to overflow while irrigating the field increases the returns on the farmer's inputs. The study collects data such as soil moisture, soil type, soil pH, crop type, and crop stage, this data will be taken using open-source sensors and open-source modules and uploaded to the cloud storage. It provides farmers the freedom of monitoring and real-time access to the field data. After analysis, the study identifies some suggestions for working in future in the technology-based irrigation. In the future crop health, health monitoring, disease detection, fertilization suggestion, and Artificial intelligence and machine learning-based decision-making based on the data.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation and Analysis of Emerging Hybrid Composite: Ramie/Kenaf/Bamboo/Pineapple
abstract: This study investigates the fabrication and analysis on the mechanical properties of a natural fiber composite material using kenaf, ramie, bamboo, and pineapple fibers to replace the synthetic fiber composite materials. The composite material is developed through a combination of fiber treatment, matrix selection, and fabrication techniques to enhance its mechanical properties, including strength, stiffness, and impact resistance. Various processing methods such as hand lay-up, compression molding are explored to optimize the composite's performance. The results indicate that each type of natural fiber exhibits unique mechanical characteristics, influencing the overall behavior of the composite materials. Ramie-reinforced composites demonstrated superior tensile strength, while pineapple and kenaf fibers exhibited excellent flexural properties. Bamboo-reinforced composites showed promising impact resistance, interface on the mechanical properties of the composite is systematically analyzed. Additionally, the biodegradability and sustainability of the composite material are assessed to ensure its environmental compatibility. The resulting natural fiber composite exhibits promising mechanical properties suitable for industrial application, offering a lightweight, durable, and environmentally friendly alternative to conventional materials.

articleTitle: Stock Price Forecasting Using LSTM Model
abstract: This research work incorporates historical data and various predictive models to forecast the future prices of stocks traded in financial markets based on factors such as market trends, company performance, economic indicators, and external events. This work introduces a new approach for the prediction of stock market using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) type of networks. It enhances the ability of model to recognize patterns and temporal connections in historical stock price data by incorporating multiple layers of LSTM units. The model can effectively learn both short-term and long-term dependencies, helping to adapt to the volatile nature of these financial markets. Rigorous experiments validate the efficacy of this stacked LSTM-based approach in predicting and understanding stock market trends. Once the models are trained and validated, it is used to make predictions on unseen or future data, generating forecasts of stock prices alongside measures of uncertainty or confidence intervals. The accuracy of the model has been increased to 98.2% using the proposed technique. Sentiment Analysis has been incorporated to include the effects of news articles etc. as positive, negative or neutral sentiment. In order to continue to explore the possibilities of machine learning in financial forecasting, our findings pave the way for further advancements in predictive modelling and risk management strategies.

articleTitle: Analyzing Handwriting Features for ADHD Detection in Children with Autism via Machine Learning
abstract: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) develops in children's brains, portrayed by symptoms of inattentiveness, hyperactivity, and impulsivity. Early identification is very much essential, but traditional diagnostic methods might be subjective in practice and consuming time. Hence this work intends to introduce an end-to-end hybrid deep-learning system which fuses the techniques CNN and Bi-LSTM Networks to develop a system using handwriting to detect ADHD in children. The Bi-LSTM layers capture the sequential dependencies that exist in the handwriting data, capturing the temporal irregularities, whereas the CNN layers extract spatial features such as stroke patterns and pressure variations. The training and evaluation of the proposed model was done by synthetically balancing the dataset with accuracy, Confusion matrix, ROC curve and AUC for assessing performance. A method that has surpassed an accuracy of 90% in classification, this proposed system has been able to properly point out ADHD-related traits by hand. This method is scalable as it approaches to do fewer computations for the detection, thus making it a real data-driven alternative to traditional methods. Future work: Add attention mechanisms to increase the model's ability toward generalization, expand available datasets, and improve generalized capabilities.

articleTitle: A Cutting-Edge Machine Learning Framework for Potato Leaf Disease Detection
abstract: Agriculture play important role in Indian economy and it provides livelihood to millions of people. Plant diseases are affecting this plant growth. If it is given timely treatment then it also works as boost of economy. The traditional methods of predicting plant diseases are extremely time-consuming and do not yield precise results. Machine learning based approach can automate the prediction of diseases in the plants. Objectives: Authors used four machine learning algorithms in the proposed work for the prediction of plant diseases, including K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Support Vector Machines (SVM), Decision Trees, and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). Dataset is taken from kaggle which is having 4062 images which are used for training and testing of these models. The images are harvested from the Central Punjab region of Pakistan and depict different stages of potato leaf diseases typical in the region. Methods: Precision, recall, and F1 score are computed in order to assess the research work. The experimental results are verified by taking comparisons between the proposed models. Results: The outcome of the research work proved that CNN model performed well among the four models. For the CNN model Accuracy is calculated at 95%, Precision is 93%, Recall is 92% and F1 score is 92%.

articleTitle: Enhancing Evidence Protection and Authenticity with Blockchain in the Judicial Sectors
abstract: The forensic evidence in the legal sector is now much more challenging to authenticate its integrity and authenticity. In fact, evidence management is easily tampered with, not authorized, and inconsistent because of the traditional systems that lack data integrity. This paper presents an end-to this challenge through the invention of using blockchain technology in evidence preservation and authentication. This paper presents a proposed system for providing an immutable and transparent chain of custody for forensic evidence using distributed ledger technologies and smart contracts. The methodology gives in detail a review of blockchain's ability to protect evidence from unauthorized access by other people as well as the ability of distributed ledgers to permit organizations to interoperate on the process of handling evidence. The results show that blockchain does not merely provide tamper-proof evidence custody but also provides an apparent and secure form of transferring custody, making judicial systems more reliable. Some of the challenges include scalability, security breaches, and regulatory compliance; nonetheless, blockchain is the revolutionary solution for enhancing forensic record storage and court documentation. This study throws the spotlight on blockchain's capability in revolutionizing the protection and authentication of evidence for criminal investigations in the future.

articleTitle: Dynamic Gesture Recognition for Sign Language Using Long Short-Term Memory Networks
abstract: A significant defect in our society is the social divide between people with disabilities and those without. Communication is one of the most significant characteristics of humans, who are thought of as social animals. One of the biggest challenges for those with hearing and vocal impairments is communication. For someone who has hearing and voice impairments, this incapacity to communicate causes regular issues and interferes with their everyday tasks. We have suggested a way to get beyond this communication obstacle in our research work. Everyone can use this solution with ease, and with a few tweaks, it can be made to function on the majority of systems having camera modules. Our method employs an integrated camera module to record hand movements in real time, based on landmarks or hand key points. Proposed LSTM based model have been evaluated in real time environment and a significant result have been reported as mentioned in the result section.

articleTitle: K-means Clustering Hybridized with Improved Chaos Based Particle Swarm Optimization for High Dimensional Problem
abstract: PSO algorithms are gaining considerable attention because of its involvement in swarm evolutionary computing. However, there are still issues in achieving a balance between exploration and exploitation. This work presents a hybridized technique that combines K-means and a revolutionary PSO-based algorithm to tackle these problems. The research introduces Chaos Adaptive Particle Swarm Optimization (CAPSO), which utilizes chaos theory to dynamically modify important parameters and a regulating factor. This approach improves the adaptability of the algorithm and prevents premature convergence of the PSO algorithm. Subsequently, the integration of K-means clustering with CAPSO is employed to expedite convergence and employ chaotic search for enhancing the Optimal Point Globally in High dimensional data. The efficiency of KCAPSO in solving difficult multidimensional problems has been confirmed by experimental findings. KCAPSO exhibits significant advancements compared to traditional K-means, rendering them highly helpful for utilization in diverse optimization endeavors.

articleTitle: Advanced AI & ML Applications in Satellite Image Processing & Industry
abstract: By integrating advanced artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) into satellite image processing, a number of industries standard to benefit in kinds of artificial intelligence and machine learning used for geoanalysis. Decades-old image processing processes are beginning to be invaded by robots. Using ML and AI to process satellite images provides a lot of new AI powered imaginations that can monitor environmental change, support disaster response and plan city layouts. Such development in the precision of techniques such as object classification, object detection and pixel detection make the analysis of image sequences from satellites possible and rapid. Enhancement of task accuracy and observability. Widely used in fields like greenhouse gas surveillance, changes in land use trends and the natural habitats of animals. In addition to introducing AI methodologies into high resolved satellite data, obvious advantages are brought to both decision making and environmental sustainability in many fields. As countries put satellites in orbit and their images become more readily accessible to the public, the opportunities for AI-driven applications of satellite image data are expected to increase, offering significant advancements in such fields as global development and resource management. This paper discusses such earth-moving applications and looks at how the future of artificial intelligence (AI) is being impacted by all this.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Model for Brain Tumor Detection
abstract: Accurate and reliable brain tumor detection is essential in medical imaging, yet challenges such as limited and imbalanced datasets hinder model performance. This project proposes a comprehensive approach to enhance detection accuracy by integrating data augmentation, synthetic data generation, and advanced machine learning techniques. Initially, we employed a CNN on a dataset derived from a recent research paper, achieving an accuracy of 90%. Leveraging transfer of learning with an already trained model, we further improved the accuracy to 94%. To address dataset imbalance, we augmented the dataset to create 1,500 images per class, increasing the total from 3,000+ to 4,500 images. We then utilized GANs to generate 500 additional synthetic images per class, resulting in a dataset of 6,000 images. By applying an optimized CNN model with techniques like batch normalization, this enhanced dataset an accuracy reaches of 98.22%.

articleTitle: Reliability Analysis of Random Component Failure in a Series Hydraulic Robot Configuration
abstract: In this manuscript, we analyse the reliability of hydraulic and electromagnetic robots using the block diagram technique, that all components form a series configuration, meaning if any components fails, the robot collapses. Hydraulic actuators are controlled by servo valves, and each limb receives this motion directly or indirectly. Robotic systems are increasingly used for inspection and maintenance due to their versatility in challenging conditions, offering worker efficiency and safety. Robotic manipulators are a significant part of these systems, as they provide a significant portion of the robots used in these settings. Robotic solutions enhance manufacturing processes in the Industrial Revolution, enhancing productivity, and reducing production cycle time, and total cost. We also analyses the failure components in the hydraulic robot system which helps the reliability of doing the proper work in the industry by a hydraulic robot and saves money and time.

articleTitle: Dynamic Resource Allocation Strategies for Cloud Computing: A User-Centric Approach Using AI
abstract: Cloud computing has simplified resource accessibility to most organizations and private individuals. It is flexible, scalable, and economical, but managing those resources can be a challenge, especially in the face of changing user demands. This study proposes a smart system that enables machine-learning algorithms in predicting and managing resources such as CPU, memory, and cost. The system, after analyzing past data files and understanding user needs, predicts workloads with an approach to resources adapted automatically. Doing so does allow resources to be managed more efficiently, thereby saving both costs and time. The system was put to test on real data files and showed clearer performance with less waiting time and cost-saving efforts while keeping the users satisfied.

articleTitle: Hybrid DNA Differential Methylation Machine Learning Technique for Prediction of Mammary Carcinoma
abstract: In many parts of the world, breast cancer is the main reason why women pass away. Until the condition has gotten too bad for appropriate therapy, the disease is frequently misdiagnosed. Consequently, minimizing mortality and other associated hazards would be aided by early disease detection. It is tricky to recognize and understand microarray gene expression data, making it difficult to assess and choose the most pertinent group of genes to use as breast cancer indicators. Here, we use a dataset and a variety of machine learning methods, like Random Forest Classification, Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine, Logistic Regression, and Logistic Regression, to create predictions about their future growth. The Breast Cancer Wisconsin Evaluation dataset and Matlab 2018 were used in our study to create a hybrid machine-learning model for quick breast cancer prediction. In comparison to other machine-learning techniques, the highly effective Gradient Boosting classifier has a success rate of 99.78%. The diagnosis, analysis, and prediction of breast cancer could all be revolutionized by this novel method of prediction.

articleTitle: Leveraging Machine Learning Techniques for Accurate Heart Disease Prediction Through Data Insights and Model Optimization
abstract: This research paper aims to develop a machine learning-based framework for heart disease prediction using critical cardiovascular health indicators. Based on a strong dataset, the study uses classification algorithms such as logistic regression, k-nearest neighbours, and random forest to model the complex relationships between clinical and demographic factors. Advanced data preprocessing and visualization techniques are included in the methodology to identify trends and correlations that may not be otherwise seen, thereby allowing a better understanding of the underlying data. The framework focuses on feature selection and hyperparameter optimisation to improve the performance of the model, thus making the prediction reliable. Various cross-validation and randomised search strategies are used for finetuning models to tackle issues with overfitting or class-imbalance distributions in data. Data visualization of features, including scatter plots or bar charts, offer actionable interpretation into how diseases manifest among the population because of variables such as age and levels of cholesterol and heart rates. With the integration of machine learning with a comprehensive analysis of data, the research will help in the early detection and prevention of heart disease. The approach proposed here can offer scalable and adaptive frameworks for clinical applications within personalized healthcare and data-driven solutions. Further directions in this area would be to increase the dataset size and real-time monitoring to be more precise in predictive and practical applicability in decision-making processes. framework for clinical applications. Future work should include increasing the dataset size and incorporating real-time monitoring to make predictions more accurate and with practical use in medical decision-making.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Suspicious Activity Detection Techniques in Surveillance Videos
abstract: The need to detect suspicious activities automatically in surveillance videos has become a significant challenge in recent time and became a hot topic for researchers to find and develop new and better techniques to solve this problem. This paper provides a detailed review of several papers and the methods used in those on anomaly detection in video surveillance using different machine learning and deep learning techniques which have been explored till now and gave promising results. CNN-based models, spatiotemporal autoencoders, object-centric autoencoders, and transfer learning-based algorithms are among the approaches examined in this paper. A comparative review of their techniques, accuracy, computing efficiency, and real-time application is presented.

articleTitle: Driver Drowsiness Detection and Alert System Using Computer Vision
abstract: Driver monitoring is essential as the main reasons for motor vehical accidents is related to driver's inattention or drowsiness. Drowsiness can cause serious road accidents resulting into a threat to life. A drowsiness detector installed on a vehicle can reduce accidents by addressing moment of negligence in real-time. The proposed system aims to assess the drowsiness, fatigue, and distraction accurately by analyzing both eye patterns and eye motion of the driver. The traditional systems can track the driver's eye state, but fail to detect dangerous situations, like a microsleep. Wheareas, the computer vision based system makes it easy to determine the moment of falling asleep, but it needs an additional logic limiting the detection range to prevent increasing a wrong blink detection rate. The proposed approach refines drowsiness detection by analyzing the blink patterns and eye movement to accurately determine when an alarm should be triggered. When drowsiness is detected an alert can be generated by the system through the speakers by playing a beep sound or by displaying an alert message on the display. Further, a system can be integrated with advanced safety features such as emergency breaking to slow down the vehicle when drowsiness is detected.

articleTitle: AgriSynth: Machine Learning - Driven Crop Intelligence, Fertilizer Rationalization and Disease Diagnostics
abstract: Agriculture is important to feeding the world's growing population, especially in the face of climate change. Machine learning technology has the potential to greatly improve agriculture by helping farmers make more educated decisions. However, current systems have considerable limitations. Many fertilizer recommendations only address the key nutrients NPK: nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium, fail to account for water availability, and rely on out-of-date historical data. This study would close these gaps by producing a machine learning system that can help farmers with crop recommendations, fertiliser guidance, and plant disease detection. The algorithm considers micronutrients and organic matter in addition to NPK when recommending fertiliser. It also incorporates water availability and real-time meteorological data to provide more precise crop suggestions, especially important for drought-prone areas. Deep learning methods analyze plant photos to detect diseases early on. Our findings indicate that by incorporating micro nutrients, water data, and real-time climate updates, the system can deliver more precise crop and fertilizer recommendations. The Random Forest and XGBoost models outperform, and the disease detection component helps to prevent crop losses by intervening early. The key takeaway from this study is that merging machine learning with large amounts of data can significantly improve farming techniques, raise crop yields, and provide farmers with reliable insights, thereby enhancing food security and sustainable agriculture.

articleTitle: Hybrid Deepfake Detection Framework: Integrating Customized CNN, Ensemble Learning, and Meta-Learning for Enhanced Robustness
abstract: Deepfake technology is widely used to generate hyper-realistic media and animated content. With its advantage, it is a challenge to detect real content as manipulated content may lead to malicious activities, defamation, and rumors. To overcome this issue, in this paper, a Hybrid Deepfake Detection Framework is proposed, in which a Customized Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), a stacking-based ensemble approach, has been integrated with meta-learning. The proposed framework has analyzed facial landmarks to extract features using multiple CNN architectures. Meta-learning has been adapted to refine and improve accuracy in the classification of fake content and real content. The proposed framework has been implemented using Celeb-DF (V2) and FaceForensics++ datasets and evaluated on performance parameters metrics Accuracy and AUC. For the Celeb-DF(V2) dataset, the Accuracy percentage is 96.33% and AUC percentage is 97.05% whereas for FaceForensics++ dataset Accuracy percentage is 97.00% and AUC percentage is 98.00%.

articleTitle: Facial Biometrics-Driven Feature Encoding and Deep Learning Integration for Secure Password Retrieval
abstract: The proposed system includes face recognition-based systems designed for secure identity verification and decentralized data storage. The working is supposed to be done in three phases: data capture, training of the machine learning model, and decentralized data storage. Collection in the first phase will include face images of individuals and government-issued identification details, such as Aadhar and PAN. A machine learning model will be trained in the second phase for improving the accuracy in the face recognition process. The third phase ensures secure storage of the recognized faces and associated personal data through a decentralized approach similar to blockchain technology. Security, privacy, and resilience against tampering are further developed in this design. The proposed system will reliably meet the application requirements that involve strong authentication processes and protection of data, therefore making the sectors using these systems include government services and secured personal data management.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Deepfake Video Detection System
abstract: Deepfake technology involves the tampering or creation of synthetic media, the technology can be highly effective in undermining trust in digital content because it exploits developments in machine learning. A new algorithm is proposed with a hybrid deepfake detection framework that integrates CNNs and RNNs with the functionalities of spatial and temporal inconsistency detection. The proposed method, using FaceForensics++ and the Deepfake Detection Challenge (DFDC), comes with a detection accuracy of 92.5%. The study addresses challenges including bias in the dataset and computational efficiency as well as model generalization. The study contributes to applications in security, content verification, and real-time monitoring on social platforms.

articleTitle: Leveraging Ensemble Methods for Robust Attack Detection in Consumer IoT Environments
abstract: Consumer Internet of Things (CIoT) enables seamless communication between smart devices but lacks robust security measures. This vulnerability exposes CIoT systems to cyberattacks like Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) and unauthorized access. Major studies indicate that traditional ML algorithms struggle with accuracy in attack detection. To address this, this paper proposes a voting classifier combining Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), KNN, and SVM to enhance cyberattack detection in complex CIoT environments. This approach reduces the limitations of individual methods and enhances robustness by utilizing their advanced capabilities. The experimental results show 96.23% detection accuracy with this novel approach outperforming the individual models and thus gives a promising solution for environment.

articleTitle: Chronic Kidney Disease: Data Clustering and Prediction Using Various Machine Learning Algorithms
abstract: A major worldwide health concern, chronic kidney disease (CKD) has a high mortality and morbidity rate and can lead to several other illnesses. Since there are no overt signs of infection in the early stages of chronic kidney disease (CKD), patients frequently miss it. Early-stage chronic kidney disease (CKD) patients have a greater chance of receiving prompt therapy to stop the infection from spreading. AI models can successfully help physicians accomplish this aim because of their quick and precise recognition execution. In this work, we propose an AI method for diagnosing chronic kidney disease. The University of California Irvine (UCI) AI collection provided a number of the missing properties in the CKD informative index. KNN ascription, which chooses a limited number of full examples with the most comparable predictions to handle each deficient example's missing data, was used to fill in the gaps. Overall, because patients may miss a few estimations for a variety of reasons, missing qualities are usually seen in clinical settings. Once the inadequate informational index was adequately rounded off, models were constructed using six AI computations: arbitrary woodlands, support vector machine, k-closest neighbor, innocent Bayes classifier, decision tree, and strategic relapse. The choice tree and irregular forests AI models outperformed the others with a 99.00% determination precision. Therefore, it is estimated that this procedure may apply to more complicated clinical data for sickness diagnosis by examining the misconceptions caused by the setup models.

articleTitle: Risk Analysis of Indian Banking Stocks Using Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: Indian banking stocks are highly volatile in nature. Although these stock values are dependent on their fundamentals. However, the banking stocks are susceptible to economic ups and downs, market sentiments, manufacturing factors and employment conditions, etc. Existing studies largely focus on implementing machine learning models for stock price prediction. However, minimal studies exist for stock risk analysis. In order to safeguard the investment of retail customers, there is a need to analyze the risk associated with them by simple tools in advance. In this paper, machine learning techniques viz. Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) are investigated to predict the banking stocks risk. The statistical risk measures used are beta and value at risk (VaR). The simulation results indicate that the least Mean Absolute Error (MAE) for beta and Value at Risk are obtained by XGBoost and LSTM techniques respectively.

articleTitle: Coronary Artery Disease Prediction Using Machine Learning
abstract: Machine learning (ML) is being widely used to help diagnose diseases and track how they progress. In this project, we used different ML techniques on the Z-Alizadeh Sani public UCI dataset, which focuses on Coronary Artery Disease (CAD). The main aim was to predict CAD using methods like Logistic Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), CatBoost, XGBoost, and LightGBM. While there are other systems for predicting CAD, many struggle with low accuracy or handling missing data. To tackle this, we used t-tests to select important features and PCA to reduce the dataset's dimensions because it had a small sample size. We tested our models using 10-fold CV, which gave us an average accuracy of over 86.02%. The models also showed precision and Fl-scores close to 90%. Among them, Random Forest performed the best, with an AUC of 87%. Overall, our approach showed promising results and performed better than previous studies.

articleTitle: Pre-contextualized Augmented Language Instructions for Autonomous Vision-and-Language Navigation
abstract: Advances in natural language has allowed for the automation of robotic tasks with minimal supervision, even in ambiguous situations. In the field of robotic navigation, human instruction can be utilized to allow a robotic agent to traverse unknown environments using instructional commands that mimic human-to-human interaction. This paper demonstrates the success of one such machine learning algorithms, delineating each machine learning architecture, and processes alternate fields where learning techniques can be applied for robotic automation.

articleTitle: Detection of Minority Attacks in IOT Devices Using Recursive Feature Elimination Technique
abstract: Effective intrusion detection systems are in high demand to protect the security and privacy of Internet of Things (IoT) devices and the networks to which they connect. In this study, we use the CICIDS2018 dataset, a widely-used benchmark for network intrusion detection in IoT environments, to investigate anomaly detection in IoT gadgets. Our objective is to identify and classify minority assault data using machine learning techniques. To do this, we employ four widely used classifiers: a Decision Tree, a Random Forest, a K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN) algorithm, and a Support Vector Machine (SVM) technique. These classifiers are trained with data from the CICIDS2018 dataset, which describes the various forms of network traffic produced by IoT devices. Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) is used to select the most relevant features and improve the models' classification performance. Furthermore, we prevent attacks against the minority group from being noticed by randomly undersampling the sample. This allows us to concentrate on accurately detecting and categorising the very few but essential attacks that represent the most risk to IoT systems. We run tests and analysis to compare the four classifiers' performance in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1- score. The effects of feature selection and data balancing on classification precision are also explored.

articleTitle: Enabling Sustainable E-Waste Management Through Blockchain Technology
abstract: E-waste is a global problem for human health and the environment; it is growing rapidly. In this study, an inventive method of managing e-waste is made possible by the combination of blockchain technology and the Internet of Things with Collector Vendor Machines (CVMs). Blockchain technology is used throughout the lifetime process, from collecting user-generated e-waste to transporting it to a recycling facility. Its decentralized and unchangeable features guarantee data security, transparency and traceability for all parties involved. To validate the blockchain data, users authenticate themselves by scanning QR codes on the CVMs container. After successful authentication of the user, it deposits the waste into the CVMs container which is equipped with an IOT load cell sensor for weight of e-waste, then transaction records are created on blockchain. The blockchain also offers smart contracts to automate tasks like data recording contracts, recycling, monitoring and reward distribution. After sending e-waste to the recycling centre, token-based reward distribution to the users, which enhances the user involvement. Using the IOT devices, the load cell sensor and microcontroller ensure real-time data and using a middleware platform offer encryption techniques that offer smooth communication between the CVMS, IOT gateway, blockchain network, handles issues regarding data privacy, scalability and security. Hence, the system provides a safe, secure and responsible platform for e- waste management practices.

articleTitle: A Novel Technique for Well-Optimized Content Replication in Fog Computing
abstract: A fog computing architecture processes huge amount of data by using edge devices. The cloud computing paradigm's fog layer helps to improve quality of service (QoS) in time-sensitive applications. Because devices at the edge of the cloud are very diverse and dynamic, content replication is vital. Replication is essential for consistent service delivery in fog computing. Time-sensitive requests received scant consideration in many of the early approaches. To improve fog computing replication, this research suggests a novel content replication mechanism using KNN and Naïve Bayes classification models. The recommended approach consists of two steps: The first assigns a failure risk classification to the fog servers that are available for replication. In the second phase, we suggest size-based content replication, in which the file or content is replicated on the less likely-to-fail fog server. We have evaluated the performance using metrics like utilization, throughput, and latency. The usefulness of the proposed strategy is validated by simulation results comparing it with the Replica-3 method. Comparing this to the Replica-3 technique, better resource usage, higher throughput, and lower latency are therefore attained. By allowing the system to handle more queries in parallel across multiple computers or processors, KNN's parallel processing capabilities of CPUs and GPUs ensures better resource utilization and greatly increasing throughput as compared to Naïve Bayes model. Additionally, KNN classification offers a useful data structure that significantly reduces latency by minimizing the time required to find the nearest neighbours.

articleTitle: sTransforming Radiology with IoT-Enabled Smart Wireless Solutions in Healthcare Infrastructure
abstract: This study aims to review the use of Internet of Things (IoT) technology for radiology applications in order to improve diagnostic accuracy, organizational workflow, and patient-centric otherwise known as patient-oriented care. The main intent is to evaluate the role of IoT solutions in changing radiology processes through wireless connectivity, intelligent diagnosis, and maintenance. Quantitative comparison of imaging performance was performed together with the qualitative data collected from healthcare practitioners. Information was gathered from IoT infused radiology systems, including real-time data exchange capabilities, equipment availability and artificial intelligence derived diagnosis. The findings point that IoT systems enhance diagnostics productivity by minimizing processing time and offer offsite diagnostics across 5G networks and the cloud. Maintenance was done based on a prediction that reduced equipment time off and analytics threw light on early diseases stages with special focus on cancer treatments. Overcoming challenges with the use of SOP and improved security of systems will go further to advance the prospect of IoT in the healthcare industry. The study will highlight the need to create and sustain practice improvement for the enhancement of resilient patient-centered radiology.

articleTitle: Bi-Directional Long Short Term Memory with Dynamic Time Wrapping for Time Series Classifications
abstract: Time series data includes both global and regional patterns. Most currently used nature networks concentrate on local features rather than their connections. The latter is likewise crucial but more problematic to investigate due to the difficulty in employing feature networks to gather enough representations. This research focus to design a new model with the help of “Dynamic Time Warping (DTW)” and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM). This model encompasses processes such as gathering data, extracting features, and performing classification. Here, DTW is used for the feature extraction to get the significant features. Then, a DTW -based extracted feature is fed to the classification stage, the classification results are obtained through the utilization of “Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory” Further, the experimental results have verified the superior performance of the designed proposed model over other existing time series classification approaches.

articleTitle: VisiCompanion: Comparative Analysis of Yolov8 and Yolov9
abstract: There are approximately 21 million visually im-paired individuals who depend on other people for their basic work. This research adds to the current understanding of assistive technology by introducing a method for choosing and optimizing the best object detection models suited for accessi-bility environments. This research enhances the Visicompanion functions and assists visually impaired individuals in doing crucial daily tasks independently by selecting a suitable model. This research compares the analysis of two models i.e. Y oLov8 [1] and YOLOV9 [2] and identifies which algorithm is best for the application. YOLOv8 is known for its rapid inference speed which is beneficial for real-time systems whereas YOLOv9 introduces advanced detection capability that improves accuracy but may increase problems for processing time and computational resource requirements. This research uses evaluation metrics like precision, recall, size of model, and resource utilization across different hardware configurations. The results showed thatYOLOv9 is slightly better than YOLOv8 with mAP reaching 95% and precision 96.8%.

articleTitle: Automated Brain Tumor Identification in MRI Scans Using State-of-the-Art Deep Learning Models
abstract: A lump or development of aberrant cells in your brain that grows unhindered is called a brain tumour. Cancer or tumours may begin in the brain or spread there from other parts of the body. Early brain cancer detection is an extremely difficult task for radiologists. Brain tumours grow quickly; they often double in size in 25 days. Patients who receive inadequate treatment typically have a survival rate of no more than six months. It can quickly result in death. Because of this, an automated approach is necessary to detect brain tumours at an early stage. This idea suggests an automated technique for quickly distinguishing between a cancer and a healthy brain using the brain's magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), two deep learning principles, are used in this research. Two models-one with two convolutional layers and the other with two fully linked layers-are displayed in this research. And the second model, which has three fully, linked layers and four convolutional layers. When testing these models, satisfactory accuracy was attained; hence, radiologists can use this method in real life to promptly identify cancers and take action that could potentially save lives.

articleTitle: Towards Precision Sports Image Classification: Insights from Weighted Ensemble Models
abstract: The precise detection of sports activities and athletic movements within images represents a complex problem because of the diversity of the sport along with the complexity of human body motions. Research development focuses on addressing this challenge by creating a sophisticated weighted ensemble model that synthesizes the leading deep-learning network components of ResNet50 DenseNet121 and EfficientNet-B0. Each of the ResNet50 Dense-Net121 and EfficientNet-B0 operates extraordinarily well when processing visual data. These separate models reach their full potential after being integrated into a weighted ensemble framework. The collective mechanism merges commission outputs while rating them according to their validation accuracy results. Through Weighted Ensemble the resulting performance achieves better accuracy than individual models thus reaching a testing accuracy of 98% which demonstrates strong capability in sports image classification. The presented research points to ensemble learning techniques including weighted ensembles as key factors which increase image classification effectiveness. The ensemble model validated its effectiveness through a 98% testing accuracy which signifies its practical value for sports analytics content recommendation systems and fitness tracker implementations.

articleTitle: Progressing Alzheimer's Diagnosis with Ensemble CNN Model
abstract: This paper proposes an Alzheimer's disease prediction model using CNN, implemented on a system with AMD Radeon Vega 8 Graphics to improve computational traceability. The research is encouraging because the implicates of the model touched the 97% accuracy of the disease prediction by MRI images of patients. The integration of the Vega 8 GPU allows the system to process large datasets and perform computations at a significantly faster rate, thereby reducing training time. The MRI dataset used in this study is highly imbalanced, with four classes: Non-Demented or Non-D, Very Mild Dementia or V.M.D, Mild Dementia or M.D, Moderate Demented or M.D.A. CNN was chosen for its capability in highlight extraction and learning from MRI pictures, without requiring human interference. The show was run with parallel and multiclass datasets, and IT got 97% exactness. The systematic analysis of the test shows that the system can diagnose Alzheimer's right at the initial stage of the disease development. This approach shows how CNNs with the aid of AMD Radeon Vega 8 Graphics perform well in automating Alzheimer's diagnosis while breaking the barriers associated with manual feature extraction and orthodox dependence on experts.

articleTitle: Satellite Image Classification Through Stable Diffusion and Vision Transformers
abstract: Various satellite images are used for scientific purposes; however, their availability is limited. To solve this problem, data augmentation is used. It is a widely used method to decrease model overfitting by increasing the number of training examples. Our goal is to increase the existing dataset while maintaining its credibility. For this, we have used stable diffusion to increase the dataset, followed by a vision transformer for image categorization. Vision transformers, in contrast to traditional techniques, divide images into patches and allow spatial connections, allowing data augmentation to expand the dataset via stable diffusion. This work provides insights into the technology architecture and training process and establishes a strong foundation for upcoming developments in the field by demonstrating the impact of ViT on satellite imagery interpretation coupled with stable diffusion. The efficiency of this model has been established as it achieved an accuracy of 99.16% in the SAT 6 dataset.

articleTitle: Multimodal Image Fusion for Enhanced Medical Diagnosis
abstract: Nowadays, image fusion has developed a dynamic meadow in image processing, specifically in medical analysis. Multimodal Medical Image Fusion (MMIF) improves medical images by merging two or more images of diverse modalities, resulting in a vibrant, and instructive fused image. Deciding on the utmost operative MMIF technique is decisive for attaining greater image eminence. The study delivers an inclusive assessment of MMIF techniques, leading medical imaging modalities, fusion steps, and valuation methodologies. Fundamental modalities consist of Computed Tomography (CT), Positron Emission Tomography (PET) and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI). MMIF techniques are classified into various transforms such as spatial domain, fuzzy logic, morphological approaches, and sparse representation methods. Furthermore, fusion may befall on pixel-level, feature-level, or decision-level fusion, through valuation alienated into subjective and objective data. The research, moreover, projects MMIF techniques, emphasizing their corresponding assets and flaws, as well as managerial specialists, concerning ideal imaging resolutions.

articleTitle: Comparison of CNN and Vision Transformers for Wildfire Detection: A Proxy for Stubble Burning
abstract: Stubble burning is a widely used agricultural practice in India and several other countries that greatly contribute to heavy air pollution. It is done to clear crop residues, usually from April to May and October to November. The gases released during this practice, including particulate matter and greenhouse gases, pose serious health and environmental risks [5]. This research focuses on classifying wildfire burning using satellite imagery as a proxy for stubble burning. We employ deep learning approaches like Convolutional Neural Networks and Vision Transformers to analyze their accuracy, computational efficiency, and real time suitability for environmental monitoring and potentially reduce wildfire burning's impact on air quality.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Automated Medical Image Diagnosis
abstract: Skin cancer remains a world health concern, and the best therapies for cure depends on early initial detection. It also explains several diagnostic techniques of skin cancer, for instance dermoscopy imaging that gives detailed skin data. Some of them include texture and color analysis which are being conducted to search for relevant data in pictures. In assessing several classification algorithms for the purpose of predicting skin cancer, this article will look at SV et al, CNN et al, and integration et al popular techniques. This particular work also explores the pros and cons of such approaches and focuses on the ways in which concerns such as large data and image quality influence prediction performance. The present review emphasizes the fact that the principles of accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity are appropriate testing practices to assess the efficacy of screening for cancer. Furthermore, concerning the issue areas, the paper includes such questions as the requirement for the increased volume and diversity of data, addressing the essential topics in the class, and information writing in algorithms.

articleTitle: A Detailed Study on Efficiency of ML Based Algorithms in Predicting Parkinson's Disease Using Audio
abstract: In this study, we analyse the various machine learning models in order to predictively diagnose the potential of the Parkinson's disease. We use a voice dataset in this study which is used to train the various machine learning models used here. The vocal parameters in the dataset are used to train our models. Our research has given us the following accuracy for each of the given models, Logistic Regression: 89.74%, SVM (Support Vector Machine): 89.74%, Decision Tree: 92.31%. Random Forest, kNN(k Nearest Neighbor) and XGBoost having the same accuracy of 94.87%. Stacking Models: 84.62% and Polynomial Features model: 94.87%. In our study, to analyse and better understand the working and the performance of the models, the metrics used by us for the evaluation of the models are: recall, precision, accuracy and F-1 score. In our research presented in this article, we have come upon the conclusion that the best performing models in the given context are Random Forest along with kNN (k Nearest Neighbor) and XGBoost. To further choose the optimal model among the many, we use a confusion matrix. In our study we have taken into consideration the gravity of the disease and leveraged the use of modern and traditional models to to improve the non invasive methods of predictive diagnosis.

articleTitle: Improved Breast Tumor Detection and Classification with Advanced Segmentation and Morphology
abstract: The breast tumor is one of the furthermost well-known types of cancer disease that is expanding worldwide and consistently contributing to a high mortality rate. It has approx. up to ninety percent chance of survival, if we found in the primary stages of tumor. The common of cases are discovered at a progressive stage, primarily due to the lengthy referral process for breast cancer specialists and the lack of public awareness of the symptoms. For the early stage recognition and handling continue to be the most effective interpolations in improving results for breast cancer, the development of harmonizing vision-based machineries. It can recognize probable malignant high-quality breast tumor diseases that transfer the hazard of emergent cancer presents major forecasts for the breast screening progression. In this paper, preserve the MRI images prominent to preprocessing of mages then extract the features and edge details, Theafter based on a segmentation and morphological algorithm find the tumor region. Identify the breast tumor using segmentation and morphological processing with this method detect in the early stages. Tumors in these images could be identified using this algorithm. Even when pre-processing is applied to images, it results in over-segmentation. Also find the Cross-Correlation and normalized Cross Correlation values based on classification technique.

articleTitle: OpportuNest - Campus Career Management System
abstract: Becoming well settled in placements is quite difficult for a student in today's job market scenario as it is very competitive. Placement cells have a lot of data regarding the students as well as job openings to be collected. Most of these methods are traditional and very slow and tend to make mistakes, because of which there are missed opportunities for both students and companies. Being completely online, the OpportuNest project will build a very efficient platform that shall focus on streamlining processes, reviewing CV s with machine automation and making predictions on placements. Highly capable modern web technolo-gies would be employed to make the entire placement process simpler, from the sophisticated machine learning algorithms on the MERN stack to assistance for administrators and placement officers. Some of the additional benefits will include ATS scoring for resume optimization, real-time data analysis for displaying metrics of performance, AI-based job matching according to skills and qualifications of the user, and improved user experience with personalized dashboards. All of that can be achieved thanks to effective, transparent, and user-friendly components in OpportuNest's career placement environment. The practice aptitude tests score based on the Random Forest algorithm to determine the placement probability, and an interview mock test feature is available on the student dashboard. For predicting future trends like those pertaining to enrollments and placements, OpportuNest uses an LSTM neural network for analyses based on patterns in historical data. All these features in OpportuNest are meant to enhance efficiency, transparency, and user experience, thus facilitating the smooth and hassle-free placement process for both administrators and students.

articleTitle: Comparing Gradient Boosting and Linear Models for Calorie Prediction
abstract: This study presents result of experiments of five models like Linear Regression Model, Ridge Regression Model, Lasso Regression Model, Random Forest Regressor, and XGBoost Regressor on prediction of calorie expenditure by exercising biology of data. The models were evaluated with respect to Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), and R2 scores. Results imply that ensemble models, particularly XGBoost Regressor, performed much better than traditional linear models. XGBoost achieved the best performance with the least MAE (12.56) and MSE (191.63), together with highest <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{R}^{2}$</tex> value of (0.96) followed in performance by Random Forest Regressor. Linear models, Linear Regression, Ridge, and Lasso, showed high error and low <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{R}^{2}$</tex> scores, indicating their limitation in taking into account the non-trivial non-linear relationships embedded in the data. These findings underscore the important of appropriate choice of machine learning techniques for accurate calories prediction and suggested ways in which linearity gave way for shallower examination by feature expansion and model optimization.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Accuracy Analysis on Online Depression Detection Using Machine Learning and Data Science
abstract: Depression is a psychological well-being disorder. As per W.H.O It has been assessed that generally 5.0% of grown-ups experience the ill effects of depression. Depression is likewise known to be one of the main sources of handicap around the world. The death toll has been increasing year after year. It has been found that various treatments for mild, moderate and severe depression exists, but it's hard to detect and determine the severity of depression accurately. Thus, Author will use diagnostic data from PHQ- 9(Patient health questionnaire) and determine accuracy of the output. Since PHQ-9 is the standardized questionnaire used by doctors and hospitals as the first step in determining the severity of depression in a patient. Author has using 4 Machine learning models: KNN, Decision Tree, Logistic regression and SVM and then cross validating those results to determine the accuracy of PHQ-9 results. These Learning models are chosen as currently they are the best type of regression models for our use case, a similarity which can be observed in heart disease classification, which has been a big reference for this paper.

articleTitle: V2I-RL: An Efficient RSU Selection Approach in VANET
abstract: Vehicular data traffic continues to increase thus the LTE networks face significant challenges in handling the high volume of vehicular communication demand, particularly in congested areas. Road Side Units (RSUs), which are strategically deployed along roadways, can alleviate network congestion by offloading traffic from the cellular network to dedicated vehicular communication channels. This offloading reduces the strain on base stations and enhances overall system capacity, reducing latency and improving throughput. In this paper, we propose a Vehicle-to-Infrastructure Reinforcement Learning (V2I-RL) approach aimed at intelligently selecting RSUs in congested areas to optimize the overall system performance in vehicular networks. Traditional communication protocols struggle to efficiently manage traffic and data transmission in high-density environments, leading to congestion, delays, and inefficient resource utilization. By leveraging reinforcement learning, our V2I-RL approach dynamically selects the most appropriate RSU based on historical traffic conditions, real-time vehicle mobility, and network load. This intelligent selection improves communication reliability, reduces latency, and enhances the overall throughput of the network, particularly in areas with high vehicular density. Our simulation results demonstrate that the proposed V2I-RL approach significantly outperforms conventional RSU selection methods, offering substantial improvements in system performance and network efficiency in urban environments.

articleTitle: An Implementation of Stochastic Resonance based Machine Translation Model for Low Resource Languages using Novel Attention Models
abstract: In this paper we have proposed a new model in which the stochastic resonance technique is used to include white noise in the cell state and hidden state vectors of the LSTM model. A novel attention calculation technique is also being used in which cell state vectors are also used for attention score calculation. Earlier only hidden state or short-term memory vectors were used or attention score calculation, but in this novel approach we have used both cell state and hidden state vectors for attention score calculation. The encoder-decoder model which we have used produces better results than earlier models on the low-resource Indian languages.

articleTitle: Non-Linear Process Identification and Control of a SISO System Using First Principle: A Real Time Case Study
abstract: In this paper a novel methodology for identifying and implementing control strategies for non-linear systems is proposed. The dynamics are modeled using a first-principle approach, and an ordinary differential equation is derived. The transfer function is approximated by the FOPTD method. An Open-loop experiment is carried out to find the FOPTD parameters. A Closed-loop control experiment is carried out to verify the models in which the IMC tuning method was used to design the controller parameters.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Classroom Engagement with Face Recognition and Attention-Based Attendance
abstract: Modern educational environments require effective and efficient systems to track attendance and participation to ensure better learning outcomes and increased productivity. Traditional systems often mark attendance automatically, regardless of the level of student engagement. This paper introduces a novel system, “Revolutionizing Classroom Engagement with Face Recognition and Attention-Based Attendance,” designed to detect multiple faces in real time and automate the process of attendance marking based on students' attention levels. In contrast to traditional methods, attendance is only recorded when students surpass a predefined attention threshold (e.g. 75%) based on their focus during the lecture. This approach fosters a more dynamic, interactive, and focused learning environment. The proposed system leverages advanced face detection and recognition techniques, integrating Haar Cascade Classifiers, Deep Learning-based Face Detection, and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) to offer robust and accurate identification even in large, diverse classrooms. Real-time video processing is handled by OpenCV, which captures and analyzes classroom footage, while NumPy processes complex numerical computations for image data. Pandas is utilized for efficient attendance logging, storing data in easily accessible CSV files. The system's attention-tracking feature is another key innovation, as it analyzes students' gaze and behavioral cues to assess their level of engagement. This ensures that attendance is only recorded when students are genuinely focused and attentive. Designed to be scalable and non-intrusive the system can be adapted to classrooms of varying sizes and is easily incorporated into existing educational frameworks. By providing accurate attendance tracking and engagement analysis, the system not only simplifies administrative tasks but also contributes to fostering a smarter, more engaging, and more productive classroom environment.

articleTitle: Diagnostic Analysis of Skin Disease Using Deep Learning
abstract: Skin diseases are common disease mostly ignored but sometimes it becomes dangerous for human being. Ignoring this is not a good sign, but most of the time it's normal to see any skin disease on human body, and its color shows the depth of the seriousness. So it is clear that the image of the skin is the core factor of diagnosis of the disease related with it. Technologies of image processing based on machine learning and ANN provide optimum approaches to find the skin disease which will help in diagnosis of the disease. Over decades of research, edge detection techniques have evolved from simple gradient-based methods to sophisticated deep learning approaches. In this paper edge detection techniques are used to diagnosis of skin disease by finding the color difference of skin from neighboring body cell and comparing it by using machine learning algorithmsand the performances are evaluated on HAM10000 skin cancer dataset. Different machine learning algorithms are used for finding the best image analysis tool for skin disease detection in medical field.

articleTitle: Role of IoT in Flash Flood Monitoring and Early Warning System
abstract: The United Nation highlighted a remarkable agenda to reduce the danger of natural disasters. It is to make the environment safe for everyone. The United Nations also acknowledged this need through the Sustainability Development Goals (SDG 11, SDG 15 & SDG 9) to reduce the impact and effect of natural disasters & sustainable disaster management & infrastructure development. Previous studies gave the solution of Data Transmission, analysis and Long-Range Network Protocol usage and the usage of IoT 3Layer Architecture but they didn't emphasize how to overcome with some serious problems as; latency and data transmission to far areas which can't be covered by various networking protocols. The current study indicates the use of IOT 5-layer architecture and its benefits in Data analysis and prediction making and reduces the latency. This paper also addressed the use of the cloud hub to transmit the warning message to the far places. On the foundation of analysis, the paper indicates the lacks and some suggestions for future works. In early Warning System in Flash Flood Monitoring, 5-layer architecture, Cloud Hub LoRa range increasing are some vital suggestions in the study. (Abstract)

articleTitle: Leveraging Support Vector Machine for Accurate Sentiment Analysis in Healthcare
abstract: Sentiment AI leverages artificial intelligence to analyze human emotions across various fields. This research focuses on understanding patient experiences with healthcare facilities by using a Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithm in machine learning. The primary goal is to train a model to analyze patient reviews, identifying key features of each facility, such as cleanliness, doctor accessibility, and patient treatment. Implemented in Python with necessary machine learning libraries, the model can extract insights from patient responses and assess their sentiments. This study aims to assist patients in selecting suitable healthcare facilities by calculating a “goodness score” for each one, representing advancements in AI and machine learning in healthcare

articleTitle: Blindviz — Intelligent Navigation and Environmental Awareness for the Visually Impaired
abstract: The blind and visually impaired people must face significant challenges while navigating their environment independently. This paper presents “BlindViz”, a mobile application specially designed to aid the visually impaired by providing real-time object detection and scene description using the latest advancements in the AI technology. This app integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) and leverages You Only Look Once (YOLOv8) for object detection, Easy Optical Character Recognition (EasyOCR) for Text Recognition and leveraging Image Segmentation for natural language scene descriptions. As the word “Activate” is spoken into the app, it takes an image, processes it, and delivers a description through an audible output. This paper outlines the development, implementation, and evaluation of BlindViz, along with the suggestions for future enhancements to improve its usability and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Social Media Sentiment Analysis Using Machine Learning
abstract: In recent years, social media has emerged as a crucial platform for public expression, enabling individuals to share opinions and sentiments on a wide range of topics. This study explores the application of machine learning techniques-Support Vector Machines (SVM), Decision Trees, Naive Bayes, and Random Forest for sentiment analysis of social media content. By leveraging a diverse dataset of user-generated posts, we aim to classify sentiments into positive, negative, and neutral categories. We evaluate the performance of each algorithm based on accuracy, providing a comparative analysis of their effectiveness. Our findings reveal that SVM significantly outperforms the other methods in terms of accuracy establishing it as the most effective model for sentiment classification in this domain. The superior performance of SVM is attributed to its capability to manage high-dimensional data and create optimal hyperplanes for classification. These results emphasize the critical importance of selecting appropriate machine learning models for sentiment analysis, especially in the dynamic landscape of social media.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning Based Algorithms for Road Feature Extraction
abstract: Extraction of road features from remote sensing images is popular research and getting accurate road features has great practical applications such as urban planning, autonomous navigation, and disaster management. Accurate road feature extraction is challenging due to variations in road surfaces, occlusions, shadows, and complex environmental conditions. Recent advances in deep learning methods have shown great performance in road feature extraction compared with machine learning. In this paper, we evaluate and compare the performance of state-of-art road feature extraction including FCN, Unet, Segner, DeepLabv3+, and DCS-TransUpernet. This analysis is performed on the publicly available Deepglobe road extraction dataset, which consists of high-resolution satellite images. We explored the strengths and limitations of these models to understand the advancements made in road feature extraction and found that transformer-based models can capture more road information. This result sets a benchmark for future research in this domain.

articleTitle: Skin Cancer Detection and Classification Using Extreme Learning Machine
abstract: Skin cancers are an abnormal growth boost of skin on the human body. It is very dangerous for humans. Even humans can also die. Most often develop when the human body is exposed to sunlight. In this case doctors can't identify easily because lots of diseases look like skin cancer like benign tumors. According to the Journal of cancer research and Therapeutics in India there are 0.5--4.8 among females and 0.04-6.2 among male skin cancer patients. Doctors are facing issues to identify skin cancer. It takes so much time. Many Researchers have developed different models for detecting skin cancer using machine Learning Algorithms and deep learning algorithms they got good accuracy also, but their algorithms running time is high that why they can't develop fast application and it's not easy to train new model. This paper presents a deep learning model for skin cancer detection and classification by using Extreme Learning Machine. This paper also develops a system software for users to detect skin cancers by clicking and selecting a picture. Users will have to click skin picture and select that image by the software and software will detect and classify that is benign or malignant. This Approach will take very less time in training the model and it will be very fast so it can be integrated with any platform like android application, windows application and web application. The model presented in the paper is for identifying only Benign tumors and malignant cancer with 99.5% accuracy.

articleTitle: An Introduction to the Three-Body Problem Optimization Algorithm: A Novel Swarm-Based Optimization Method
abstract: The Three-Body Problem Optimization Algorithm (3BPOA) is a metaheuristic method inspired by how gravity interacts if there are three bodies, a classical physics problem. 3BPOA uses 3 best agents or leaders where these 3 best agents will interact with each other and also influence the movement of the swarm. The interaction of these 3 best bodies or agents is also influenced by the distance between the three. In this study, 3BPOA was tested on the Rastrigrin mathematical function using various scenarios from 5 dimensions to 100 dimensions, also using various population sizes.
