articleTitle: Enhanced Footpath Segmentation Using Attention-Integrated UNET For Assistive Urban Navigation
abstract: This study presents an advanced deep-learning ap- proach to enhance navigation in visually impaired individuals in urban environments. We employed a modified UNET architecture integrated with spatial and channel attention mechanisms for semantic segmentation to distinguish footpaths from other urban features effectively. The model was trained from a dataset of 3000 high-quality images, and it had an IoU of 89.82% on the test set, which exceeded the baseline model by 4.5%. We demonstrated the robustness of the model to adverse settings, including Gaussian noise and blurring, by maintaining an IoU greater than 85.32 %. When implemented in a prototype assistive navigation system, the model provided real-time feedback with 50 ms per image inference time, a far more rapid inference time that significantly increased user autonomy. In addition to advancing semantic segmentation techniques, this study also features a practical application for visually impaired navigation.

articleTitle: An Efficient Deep Learning Framwork for Classification and Detection of Anomaly Based Network Intrusion using NSL-KDD Dataset
abstract: The past few years have seen unprecedented growth in the realms of technology and networking, as well as the proliferation of Internet services across all industries and regions. Because of rising instances of piracy and the compromise of several cutting-edge systems, it is crucial that we build information security tools capable of identifying emerging threats. An Intrusion Detection System (IDS) that use deep learning (DL) methods to identify network anomalies is a crucial piece of information security technology. The purpose of this study is to look at DL techniques and see if they can be used in an anomaly-based IDS. The purpose of this research is to employ a hybrid model Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), & and (Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) to identify the unknown assault package in a state-of-the-art IDS with high network performance. Standard classification metrics were used to evaluate DL models trained on the NSL-KDD dataset. These metrics included recall, f1- score, precision, and accuracy of categorization. We used the NSL-KDD dataset to fit and assess the flow. The model's outstanding producing abilities and excellent incursion identification performance are made possible by these data characteristics. Attack detection in the NSL-KDD dataset may be accomplished in two ways: binary classification and multiclass classification. Positive outcomes have been seen when applying the suggested strategy to multiclass classification (98% accuracy) and binary classification (99.99 percent accuracy). IDS have shown encouraging results from experiments using deep IDS models. According on the results of the research, the proposed approach outperforms the competing methodologies.

articleTitle: Real-Time Driver Drowsiness Detection Using Mobile Net for Road Safety Enhancement
abstract: Research shows that fatigue ranks within the three main road accident causes worldwide. This paper develops a driver sleep detection system in real time with MobileNet as the light weight convolutional neural network architecture built specifically for indoor and mobile environments. Real-time system facial scans seek driver indicators of drowsiness which include lengthy eye closures and slow yawn activity leading to sleepiness. MobileNet operates at a low cost which makes it both rapid and functional for vehicle implementation without accuracy compromises. The system helps prevent driver fatigue which leads to better vehicle safety because drivers receive instant feedback through this alert model. This solution presents several advantages such as affordability as well as mobility through mobile devices which makes it ideal for current vehicle safety requirements. Fatigue signs to avoid accidents. When drowsiness accelerates the slowdown of reaction times but increases alertness it causes higher risks of vehicle crashes. System implementations that depend on physical signals need drivers to maintain close positions with the equipment which results in driver distraction. We evaluate the driver eye movement behavior to measure driver behavior through imaging-based dataset measurements in this paper. MobileNet eliminates optical images successfully at a low cost thus speeding up the visual fatigue relief process. MobileNet model demonstrated a performance of 94 % in the evaluation results. The system requires 0.00829 seconds to recognize tiredness. The system delivers exceptional real-time functionality thus making it an extraordinary example. Better performance was achieved through the implementation of hyperparameter optimization in connection with k fold validation. The study matters greatly because its implementation would assist in protecting lives by presenting an effective strategy to stop road fatalities arising from unpredictable seizures.

articleTitle: Converging Realms: Exploring the Intersection of the Internet of Everything (IoE) and the Internet of Metaverse (IoM)
abstract: The emergence of Metaverse, is regarded as the future of the internet and the next invention of digital experiences, often known as ‘NextG’ or ‘Web 3.0’. The theory of the IoM embodies a vision of a digital realm that is more interconnected, immersive, and interactive that goes beyond the traditional web. The 10E and IoM are interconnected as they build on each other and form a strong digital ecosystem that provides an immersive digital experience. Through integrating technologies for instance, Virtual Reality (VR), Augmented Reality (AR), Mixed Reality (MR), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and Blockchain (BC), the IoM can modernize education, commerce, communication, entertainment, and many more domains. IoM facilitates a seamless fusion of physical and virtual realms, permitting users to interact with digital environments and objects while actively interacting with others in real time. IoM aims to offer a transformative digital space that enables individuals to create, explore, engage, express, and connect in an unimaginable environment that feels real. Despite the emergence of IoM, it introduces new challenges and potential security and privacy threats to users that must be addressed.

articleTitle: A Noble Approach to the Object Detection in Defense System in Terms of Image Processing
abstract: Object identification is very important for modern defense systems because it helps ensure security and extends support in various operations. Realistic images come with issues of low contrast, motion blur, and noise, which ultimately affect detection performance. This research seeks to come up with ways of enhancing a procedure that enhances image quality and consequently detection. The method used here applies Histogram Equalization and Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) to improve the contrast. Then, Gaussian Blur & Median Blur are used to mimic and reduce the motion blur effect and eliminate noise respectively. Finally, sharpening is done to highlight edges. As a result, the image quality has significantly improved. Sharper edges, improved contrast and less noise will help in better AI detection. In the future, we plan to add machine learning models to support real-time detection which will make the system adaptable to complex environments.
